items.title: The Strait of Hormuz is largely closed to shipping
summary: On 28 February 2026, war involving Iran led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.

UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) reports that about a third of the world's seaborne fertilizer trade and about a quarter of its seaborne oil normally pass through the strait, and that ship transits fell by about 95% in March.

The World Bank reports that by April 2026 its fertilizer price index had reached its highest level since October 2022. In September 2026, researchers writing for CGIAR reported that fertilizer shipments out of the Persian Gulf remained largely halted.

reach.title: Fertilizer prices
reach.text: Canada mines more potash than any other country and makes much of its own nitrogen fertilizer, but Canadian farmers pay world prices. In March 2026 The Western Producer reported that world urea prices had jumped about 40%. Higher prices raise the cost of next year's crops.

reach.title: Phosphate fertilizer
reach.text: Sulphur from Gulf oil and gas plants is a raw material for phosphate fertilizer, so phosphate prices can rise even where the fertilizer itself is not shipped through the strait.

reach.title: Fuel
reach.text: Higher oil prices feed into diesel for tractors, trucks and trains, and into the cost of moving food.

reach.title: Possible gains
reach.text: Canadian potash and nitrogen producers may sell more abroad at higher prices. Gains and losses will not fall on the same people.

watch.title: Ships through key sea lanes
watch.text: Ships through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 3 a day over the four weeks to 22 November 2026. In the same weeks of the past five years the typical figure was about 83 a day. That is below the range of every one of those years, about 96% below the typical level. Also unusual: Bab el-Mandeb Strait (fewer ships than usual).

watch.title: World fertilizer prices
watch.text: In October 2026, the World Bank's fertilizer price index stood at 148 (2010 = 100), 6% higher than a year earlier. Prices: DAP US$803 a tonne; Urea US$420 a tonne. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is about 8% below the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. Taking every line in this panel together, one is outside the range of past years.

watch.title: What farmers pay for inputs
watch.text: In the quarter starting April 2026, the prices Canadian farmers paid for all inputs stood at 187 on Statistics Canada's index (2020 = 100), 11% higher than a year earlier. Fertilizer alone was 24% higher. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years. It is about 20% above the typical level. It is rising a little faster than usual for this time of year, but not enough to stand out. A new high or low on a figure that climbs year after year is the normal state, not a warning: it is the pace that would make it one. Taking every line in this panel together, three of the four are moving unusually fast and one is outside the range of past years.

watch.title: Diesel prices
watch.text: Diesel at self-serve pumps averaged 262.9 cents a litre across five cities in October 2026, 71% more than a year earlier. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years, after allowing for inflation. It is about 51% above the typical level. It is rising much faster than usual for this time of year. Both checks agree, so this one is worth a closer look.

watch.title: World food and energy prices
watch.text: In October 2026, the World Bank's food price index stood at 122 (2010 = 100), 15% higher than a year earlier. Energy prices were 89% higher than a year earlier. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is rising much faster than usual for this time of year. It has not yet passed the range of past years, so this is the earlier of the two signals. Taking every line in this panel together, two of the five set off both checks.

watch.title: The Canadian dollar
watch.text: One US dollar cost $1.42 Canadian on average so far in November 2026, 1.0% more than a year earlier. A weaker Canadian dollar makes imported food and farm inputs dearer. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years. It is about 4% above the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. A new high or low on a figure that climbs year after year is the normal state, not a warning: it is the pace that would make it one.

live.label: Ships through the Strait of Hormuz
live.source_note: Estimated from ships' tracking signals by the International Monetary Fund's PortWatch. The shaded band is the range for the same weeks in the past five years.
live.text: Still showing in the data: about 3 ships a day in the latest reading to 22 November 2026, against a typical about 83 ships a day for this time of year.
